questions.stem: What is the main function of the nervous system?
choices: To control and coordinate body functions
questions.solution: The main function of the nervous system is to control and coordinate body functions. It is responsible for receiving sensory information, processing it, and generating appropriate responses. This system includes the brain, spinal cord, and nerves, which work together to regulate various bodily activities.

questions.stem: The gap between two neurons is called a
questions.solution: The correct answer is synapse. A synapse is the gap between two neurons where signals are transmitted. Dendrites are the parts of a neuron that receive signals, axons are the parts that carry signals away, and impulses are the electrical signals themselves.

questions.stem: What is the function of receptors in our body?
questions.solution: The correct answer is They detect stimuli. Receptors in our body detect stimuli such as light, sound, and touch, and send this information to the nervous system. They do not carry electrical impulses, release hormones, or regulate metabolism.

questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of a voluntary action?
choices: Salivating at the smell of food
Closing the eye when an object approaches
questions.solution: Walking in a straight line is a voluntary action because it involves conscious control and decision-making. Salivating at the smell of food, closing the eye when an object approaches, and pupil shrinking in bright light are all automatic responses that occur without conscious thought.

questions.stem: Which type of movement in plants is caused by growth?
choices: Quick movement in response to touch
Directional movement in response to stimuli
Movement that occurs without any change in cell structure
Movement that happens instantly when touched
questions.solution: Directional movement in response to stimuli is caused by growth, as plants gradually adjust their growth direction based on external factors like light or gravity. Quick movement in response to touch and movement that happens instantly when touched are rapid responses not involving growth. Movement that occurs without any change in cell structure is also not related to growth, as it does not involve cellular changes.

hi.stem: पौधों में किस प्रकार की गति वृद्धि के कारण होती है?

hi.solution: उत्तेजना के प्रति दिशात्मक गति वृद्धि के कारण होती है, क्योंकि पौधे बाह्य कारकों जैसे प्रकाश या गुरुत्वाकर्षण के आधार पर अपनी वृद्धि की दिशा को धीरे-धीरे समायोजित करते हैं। स्पर्श के प्रति तीव्र गति और स्पर्श के कारण तत्काल गति वृद्धि के बिना तेज प्रतिक्रियाएं हैं। कोशिका संरचना में कोई परिवर्तन बिना गति भी वृद्धि से संबंधित नहीं है, क्योंकि इसमें कोशिकीय परिवर्तन नहीं होते।

questions.stem: What happens when a person blocks their nose while tasting sugar?
questions.solution: When a person blocks their nose while tasting sugar, the taste becomes weaker. This is because the sense of taste is enhanced by the sense of smell, and blocking the nose reduces the ability to detect the full flavor of the substance. The taste buds on the tongue detect basic tastes, but the overall perception of flavor is influenced by the olfactory receptors in the nose.

hi.stem: जब कोई व्यक्ति चीनी का स्वाद लेते समय अपनी नाक बंद कर देता है तो क्या होता है?
hi.solution: जब कोई व्यक्ति चीनी का स्वाद लेते समय अपनी नाक बंद कर देता है तो स्वाद कमजोर हो जाता है। ऐसा इसलिए होता है क्योंकि स्वाद की भावना गंध की भावना द्वारा बढ़ाई जाती है, और नाक बंद करने से पदार्थ के पूर्ण स्वाद की अनुभूति करने की क्षमता कम हो जाती है। जीभ पर स्थित स्वाद ग्राही मूल स्वादों की पहचान करते हैं, लेकिन स्वाद की समग्र अनुभूति नाक में स्थित गंध ग्राही द्वारा प्रभावित होती है।

questions.stem: Which type of plant movement is caused by the change in water content of cells?
questions.solution: The movement of leaves of the sensitive plant is caused by changes in the water content of cells, which leads to swelling or shrinking. This type of movement is classified as nastic movement. Phototropism is growth towards light, hydrotropism is growth towards water, and thigmotropism is growth in response to touch. None of these match the described mechanism.

questions.stem: What happens to a muscle cell when a nerve impulse reaches it?
questions.solution: When a nerve impulse reaches a muscle cell, the cell changes shape and shortens due to the interaction of actin and myosin filaments, which slide past each other during contraction. Expanding in size, becoming rigid, or releasing oxygen do not occur as direct results of a nerve impulse. These changes are not part of the normal process of muscle contraction.

questions.stem: Why is the movement of a sensitive plant different from the movement of an animal?
choices: Because the plant's movement is due to growth
Because the plant's movement is controlled by the brain
Because the plant's movement is due to electrical impulses
Because the plant's movement is voluntary
questions.solution: The movement of a sensitive plant is different from the movement of an animal because it is due to growth. Unlike animals, plants do not have nervous or muscular tissues to control their movement. Instead, their responses to stimuli, such as touch, are due to changes in turgor pressure, which is a result of water movement in the cells. Animals, on the other hand, rely on nervous and muscular tissues for movement.

questions.stem: In which part of the brain are decisions made about how to respond to sensory information?
questions.solution: The fore-brain is responsible for processing sensory information and making decisions based on that input.
